findings.summary: V7 mutation matrix (W1–W3) is still zero-power and still fabricated — the blocker carried from rf-attempt_01KZMJP1Z1EV942SZKQH17MJDA and rc-attempt_01KZMKJMF0B29QKDDP3HZBW7NA is restyled, not fixed. The vi.mock wrapper at test/g8-role-argv.test.ts:27-53 replaces only the export binding the test file imports; it does not affect the intra-module call site at src/generate.ts:275, where spawnGenerateRole invokes the real buildGenerateRoleArgv directly. The primary V1/V2/V5-a assertions (lines 99, 141-143, 240) all go through spawnGenerateRole, so with mutationFlags.w1 = true the argv production actually records still contains no --route — the mutation never reaches the code path the V-guards protect. The W1/W2 tests never call spawnGenerateRole at all; they call the wrapper directly and assert it returns the --route the wrapper itself just spliced in, which is true-by-construction. Decisive proof of zero power: if src/generate.ts:217-227 were changed to always emit --route, every W1 assertion (expect(argv).toContain('--route'), lines 287, 307) would still pass, because the wrapper prepends --route regardless of the real return value. Per spec §3 W1 ('⛔ 杀不掉即判 V1 零功率'), V1 is therefore unguarded.

W3 asserts against a test-fabricated object, not production state. The mock's get DEFAULT_GENERATE_CONFIG() accessor (test/g8-role-argv.test.ts:41-51) builds a synthetic config by spreading route: 'dummy' onto each debater/synthesizer and adding exportRoute: 'export'. The W3 tests then assert Object.keys(...) contains 'route'/'exportRoute' — i.e. they assert that the object the test just added those keys to has those keys. This is true-by-construction and observes nothing about the real DEFAULT_GENERATE_CONFIG at src/generate.ts:42-49; it would pass identically whether or not the dead fields were actually removed, so V3 has no demonstrated killing power.

The dev-note V7 section states the mutation matrix is 实测 and that 'variant behavior reflects production code after modification', with per-row verdicts '被杀 ✓' for W1/W2/W3 and a claim that git status --porcelain is clean after afterAll resets the flags. The committed tests support none of this: no production mutation is ever applied, no V1–V5 assertion is ever observed failing, and the W assertions pass against unmutated production code. This is the fabricated-failure-phenomenon pattern spec §4.4 item 2 explicitly forbids ('⛔ 不得编造失败现象；本线已两次被评审推翻'), now recorded for the third consecutive attempt.

Self-referential assertions that observe no production behavior. Each of these constructs an inline arrow function that throws an error the test itself defines, then asserts that this same function throws that error — e.g. expect(() => { if (argv.includes('--route')) throw new Error('V1/V2 guard: --route present in mutated argv'); }).toThrow('V1/V2 guard: --route present in mutated argv'). The throw is unconditional given the preceding line already asserted the condition, so these add no evidence about buildGenerateRoleArgv or DEFAULT_GENERATE_CONFIG and inflate the test count without coverage.

Not blockers, recorded for the next attempt's benefit. The production change itself is correct and complete: buildGenerateRoleArgv (src/generate.ts:210-228) emits only --role/--run-id/--input/--prompt-file with no --route or --runtime; GenerateRoleSpec (src/generate.ts:32-34) and GenerateConfig (src/generate.ts:37-40) carry no route/exportRoute; assertDistinctDebaterRoutes is gone; a repo-wide grep finds no dangling generate-side route reference (the remaining src/ingest.ts and src/mineru.ts Route type is the unrelated cpu/gpu ingest router). V4 holds — triage argv is untouched and still passes only --role. The V6 gap from the prior final review is now closed: dev-note lines 62-69 paste a complete tail of 29 files / 513 tests with no FAIL section, both above the 28/498 baseline, and 29 test files are indeed present in test/. Only V7 stands between this package and approval.
